text:
Alex Chen: quick heads-up — on a customer private deploy (eu-west1, onprem gateway) we saw KMS decrypt calls that never show up in our central audit pipeline. can someone triage?
Mira Patel: interesting. are these direct calls to cloud KMS or routed through our keystore-proxy?
Alex Chen: routed through keystore-proxy (edge), so the agent calls proxy -> proxy calls KMS. the proxy logs show a successful call id=kc-9f2, but audit stream missing the decrypt event.
Jordan K.: did you check local syslog export? sometimes the proxy emits but the forwarder drops due to meta tag mismatch.
Alex Chen: yeah, local logs have the entry: `INFO keystore-proxy: decrypt ok key=redwood-prod-1 req_id=kc-9f2`. forwarder shows `200` but no audit envelope.
Luca R.: this smells like envelope tagging. security-bot: query-audit-mapper kc-9f2 ->?
security-bot: mapping check: kc-9f2 -> proxy-host-11 -> forwarded with tag `deployment:private` -> last-hop acked. No audit_envelope_created event in pipeline.
Mira Patel: could be a rule in the pipeline that filters out decrypt verbs for private tenants to avoid PII in logs. but we should still emit metadata (who, when, truncated).
DevOps: we recently merged a patch that suppressed verb payloads for `decrypt` in priv deployments (MR #788). maybe that dropped the envelope entirely by mistake.
Jordan K.: if MR #788 returned null for payload it might also have returned null for the whole envelope when an allowlist check failed. can we repro on staging by forcing the proxy to emit verbose?
Alex Chen: repro steps I used: 1) ssh to edge host 11 2) curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/decrypt -d '{"kid":"redwood-prod-1","ct":"..."}' 3) observe local proxy log line above and check `audit-forwarder` output.
Mira Patel: patch suggestion: ensure audit-forwarder always emits an audit stub: `{"action":"decrypt","actor":"service-account","result":"ok","key":"<id>"}` even if we redact payload. minimal stub is sufficient for compliance.
Luca R.: agree. also need to verify network policy/routing can't bypass the forwarder. are there iptables or egress rules that let the proxy talk directly to KMS without going through the sidecar that emits audit?
Jordan K.: good point. on some onprem installs customers put a NAT rule that lets the proxy bypass the sidecar. we should detect that at startup and warn. maybe a health-check that asserts `127.0.0.1:5001` (auditor) reachable.
sre-oncall: can we add an automated check to the deploy-runbook? small `curl` against auditor endpoint with retries, fail if unreachable. I'll add to runbook.
DevOps: for network policy we can suggest a simple CNI/policy snippet to force proxy -> auditor path. example:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: force-auditor-e2e
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore-proxy
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: audit-forwarder
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 5001
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
```
Mira Patel: also recommend an attestation log that records that the forwarder handshake succeeded at boot. store attestation in local sealed storage with monotonic counter.
Alex Chen: on the KMS side, can we add a `x-audit-witness` header that the KMS echoes back, and we proof-write that to the customer's audit store? helps prove end-to-end.
Luca R.: we need to be careful: some KMS vendors strip custom headers. fallback: sign a short witness object with our tenant key and write to audit store pre- and post-KMS call.
Jordan K.: for incident response, if we ever see missing envelopes, we should: 1) snapshot local proxy logs 2) snapshot forwarder queue 3) collect netpol/iptable config 4) escalate to sec oncall. Add this checklist to the incident doc.
Mira Patel: I created a short checklist draft and pushed to the internal runbook repo (link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/keystore-audit-missing). please review.
Alex Chen: thanks — can someone own the MR to emit audit stubs? I'll open a follow-up for the network-policy enforcement and attach the repro.
DevOps: I'll take the MR for audit stubs (starting in the morning). assigning to @DevOps.
security-bot: note added to backlog: AUDIT-PRIV-1023.
Alex Chen: perfect. quick follow: could we add a small egress test to the CI that simulates a misrouted NAT and fails the test if forwarder is bypassed?
sre-oncall: yes — I'll prototype a harness that manipulates iptables in a test namespace to verify the path.
Luca R.: thanks all. let's sync tomorrow 10:00 PT for a quick 20m to align on MR and runbook edits. :calendar:
